result.summary: The kitchen sink leak at 7 Mill Lane is active and getting worse, so I treated it as an emergency. I emailed the tenant containment advice and escalated to a human at high priority. I did not pay or close anything. Riverside Plumbing's £165 invoice asks for payment to a new bank account by email, the tenant says nobody came, and invoice.pdf never arrived, so it can't be paid until it's verified. The landlord's "pay out of the rent and close it" conflicts with a leak that is still going, and his statement that the tenant has moved out conflicts with the tenant's report.
result.situation: Riverside Plumbing says the job is done and invoices £165 with changed bank details (new payee name: R Plumbing Services). The landlord says the tenant left last Friday and wants it paid from rent and closed. The tenant (Hannah Reid) says the leak is worse, there's water in the cupboard, the base is going soft and nobody came on Tuesday. The CRM has placeholder contacts, no contractor, no approvals and no invoice attachment.

The contractor claims the job is done and wants £165 paid to a new account, but the tenant says nobody came and no invoice arrived. escalation.recommendation: Phone the tenant now and book an urgent verified plumber, notifying the landlord. Freeze payment and check the bank change by phoning the contractor on a number already on file. Reconcile occupancy with the landlord. Add the address and contact details to the CRM.
